Thirteenth Indian Expedition to Antarctica, Scientific Report, 1997 
Department of Ocean Development, Technical Publication No. 11. pp. 1-20 
The Thirteenth Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica: 
An Introduction to the Expedition and Achievements 
G. SUDHAKAR RAO 
Leader 
The Thirteenth Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica was formally 
flagged off on 7th December 1993 by Dr. Wilfred D'Souza, Honorable Chief 
Minister of Goa at Marmagoa Port in the presence of Deputy Speaker of Goa 
Assembly, Shri Simon D'Souza, Dr P Rama Rao, Secretary DOD and DST, 
many dignitaries from national laboratories, Army, Navy, expedition members, 
their families, friends and other well wishers. An encouraging message on the 
eye of departure of the XIII Antarctic Expedition from the Union Minister of 
State for Ocean Development, Shri Eduardo Faleiro was read on his behalf by 
Dr P Rama Rao, Secretary, DOD. The 58 members team drawn from 1 3 
scientific organizations viz , IMD, IIG, NPL, PRL, GSI, NGRI, OU, SOI, 
NEERI, NIO, AIIMS, R&DE(E) and DEAL, and defence services viz, Army, 
Navy and Armed Forces Medical Services. The ship MV Stepan Krashenin-
nikov actually left the Marmagoa port in the afternoon of 8 Dec 93 only after 
receiving the delayed cargo (NPL laser heterodyne hut material and the newly 
acquired mantis crane). With a halt of about two days at Port Louis for taking 
fuel for ship, fresh vegetables and other items, the ship feached Antarctica on 
30th Dec 93, but could not be moored due to continuous sheet of fast ice. The 
ship started breaking fast ice on the same day and after about two days of 
continuous operations, ship moored along ice shelf in India Bay on 2nd Jan 94, 
First landing of the expedition a t Maitri with parcels and mail for X 
wintering team members was made on 31 Dec 93 around 1100 hrs. Summer 
camp and scientific induction started on 1st Jan 94 and after completion of all 
summer scientific tasks the summer camp closed on 24th Feb 94. The ship 
started sailing back on March 12, 1994 and reached Durban, South Africa on 
April 4, 1994. Due to some technical problems to the ship, the summer team 
along with X winter team members were air-lifted from Durban to Bombay 
leaving the ship in Durban for repairs. 
XIV expedition's team arrived at Maitri on January 13, 1995 to end the 
isolation of XI winter team. XIV Expedition's ship, M.V. Polar Bird along with 
2 G . Sudhakar Rao 
XIV Summer & XI Winter Teams left Antarctica on March 06, 1995 and 
reached Goa on March 29, 1995, thus ending the expedition. 
Voyage 
The ship MV Stepan Krasheninnikov is charted for the first time for the 
Indian Antarctic expedition. They were not knowing our requirements and 
initially there were many problems for the expedition members in getting 
adjusted with the facilities available in the ship like non fitting of power plugs, 
non availability of sufficient drinking water, language barrier between expedi-
tion members and most of crew members etc. Hence one register was kept in 
the lounge and members were asked to write their problems in the register. 
Almost daily there were two meetings, first with captain and his officers 
and engineers, and second with expedition members. In the first meeting 
problems used to be discussed and solutions found. In the second meeting, 
solutions to problems were told to expedition members. Help and cooperation 
from the Captain and his crew was excellent in settling of the problems. In some 
cases there was some delay because of some communication gap, but most of 
the problems used to get solved in a day or two. Meanwhile, to remove the 
language barrier, some basic Russian language classes were arranged for the 
expedition members, and English language classes for crew members, which 
was of immense help towards understanding of each other. People started 
mixing with each other and wishing each other in English and Russian. To bring 
all the members o n board the ship into still close harmony, exchange of 
members between expedition mess and crew mess for dining was arranged. By 
the time the ship reached Antarctica, all the problems of the members were over 
and there was no identity like expedition and crew members, and they started 
sharing both pleasures and pain together. 
Scientific activities of IMD, AIIMS and DEAL started from the day the 
ship left Goa. Others were not having much scientific work until they reached 
Antarctica. To keep all members busy and to use spare time fruitfully, varieties 
of activities and celebrations were arranged. Members were encouraged to do 
some physical activity daily like physical exercise, yoga etc. Birthdays and 
marriage anniversaries of members were celebrated. Besides this, the Equator 
crossing ceremony, polar circle crossing ceremony, Xmas, New year eve, 
Indian Republic day celebration, taking over of Maitri station by XI winterteam
